examples.raw: u=ḥa=yawmo aṯyo žənəke sawto, w faqərto, mlaʕela w ṭləbla meni, i=awday-aṯe ‘eines Tages kam eine alte, arme Frau und bat mich inständigst um dieses Zimmer’; 2/64;
k-milaʕət d-oṯət ʻdu wünschest sehnlichst zu kommenʼ; 424;

examples.turoyo: omər: "Ma lə gbatli u mašruqawo, gdobenux klabṯo?" Omər: "Bele, ašər, komilaʕeno. I klabṯo gəmḥamyo aʕ ʕezayḏi mad dewe."
examples.translation: (The bird) said: "Won't you give me that flute, and I will give you a dog?" He said: "Yes of course, I beg you, a dog will protect my goats from wolves."
examples.note: 2018_06_20_au_001_NE_Old_lady_n_bird: 43 komilaʕeno doṯeno koraxno ʕal i+tərto ‘I wish very much to come and look for the (lost) cow’ (Ilyas p.c.)
